text: The property lost 25.5 hectares of tree cover in 2015 due to natural or anthropogenic factors not specified in the data. The tree cover loss was observed by the University of Maryland's Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13), which tracks changes in tree cover with a canopy density of 30% or more. The European Commission Joint Research Centre's Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset corroborated that there was no forest cover in that area by 2020. The exact cause of the tree cover loss cannot be determined from the provided data, but it could be due to deforestation, logging, natural disasters, or other factors.
